jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Applied
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Trace

Trace Labs is building the data infrastructure for physical AI.

Physical AI has the potential to transform how work gets done in the real world, from robotics to embodied systems that can see, move, and interact with their environment. But today, progress is held back by one big gap: there’s no scalable way to collect high-quality, real-world training data. Frontier robotics models are trained on far less data than language models, because there’s no “internet of robotics data.”

Trace exists to change that. We capture how humans actually interact with the physical world, at scale, and we build the ML systems that make every hour of that data more valuable.

We’re an early, deeply technical team. We move fast, we care about quality, and we believe the teams with the best data will build the best robots.

The role

This role sits between ML engineering and research. You’ll bring strong ML engineering skills, a research mindset, and deep learning fundamentals to the hardest problems we see coming at Trace, then ship the answers into production.

You’ll work closely with our computer vision team, but this role is broader and more product-focused. You won’t live on one type of data. One month you might be working with sensor signals, the next with hand tracking video, the next with language. What matters is getting a high-quality model working fast and putting it to use.

We care much more about what you’ve built and shipped than where you’ve published. If you’re earlier in your career but have a clear track record of moving fast and owning hard problems, we want to talk.

What you will do

  • Own models end to end: data, training, evaluation, and deployment into our annotation pipeline.

  • Build training pipelines for large, multimodal datasets, including video, sensor streams, and language.

  • Partner with our Head of Engineering and the CV team to get models into production and keep them improving.

  • Start with the simplest approach that works, then make it better. Pull from recent papers when they help you ship, not as the end goal.

  • Move quickly between very different problems, and build the tooling you need along the way.

What we're looking for

  • A BS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, Aerospace, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. An MS is a plus, not a must.

  • 2+ years of industry of hands-on experience training deep learning models on real-world data, at a company, startup, or national lab. Earlier in your career is okay if your track record shows it.

  • Strong proficiency in Python and a modern deep learning framework such as PyTorch or JAX.

  • A solid grounding in ML fundamentals, including architectures, optimization, loss design, and evaluation.

  • Comfort with messy, real-world data such as video, time series, or sensor streams.

  • An extraordinary bias toward shipping. You go from idea to working model fast, and you make good calls under uncertainty.

  • High agency. You find the problem, own it, and get it done without waiting to be told.

  • Range. You’re excited to work across different kinds of data and problems, not just one narrow specialty.

Why Trace Labs

  • A foundational problem. The data layer for physical AI is still being defined. You’ll help define it.

  • Data at scale from day one. We have the resources to collect it. Your job is to make it count.

  • Real ownership. Your models ship into production and directly shape what our data can do.

  • Room to grow. Go deeper into ML, take on bigger systems, or both.

jobs.title: Researcher
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Trace

Trace is building the data infrastructure that lets robots learn from the real world

AI is moving into the physical world. It has the potential to transform how work gets done in the real world, from robotics to embodied systems that can see, move, and interact with their environment. But today, progress is constrained by a fundamental limitation: there is no scalable way to collect high-quality, real-world training data. Frontier robotics models are trained on orders of magnitude less data than language models because there is no equivalent of an "internet of robotics data."

Trace exists to change that.

We build the infrastructure that makes it possible to capture and transform real-world data like humans performing physical work, and turn it into training data for robots and other intelligent systems that operate outside the browser and in the physical world.

If we succeed, we will meaningfully accelerate the development of physical AI and expand what these systems can safely and reliably do in the world. If you want to be an early hire at a company helping define how robots learn to work, keep reading.

Why Trace

  • A world-changing problem: Physical AI will reshape entire industries, but it cannot scale without real-world data. Trace is addressing one of the core constraints holding the field back.

  • Early with real traction: Demand for real-world data is exploding as we start to see the impact of intelligent physical systems.

  • Experienced, tight-knit team: Ex-founders and operators with a track record of building and scaling together.

  • Real ownership: This is early. Your research will materially shape what the company trains, how it evaluates progress, and where it invests next.

  • A research team, not a publication pipeline: We care about work that makes our systems better. You'll be close to real data and real deployment.

The Role

We're hiring a researcher to join Trace and work on the core problems in robot learning: what data quality means in the paradigm of robot learning. You’ll work on how to structure real-world data for training, how to train and evaluate models on it, and how to close the loop between what we capture and what makes physical AI systems better.

This role reports to our Chief Scientist. You'll be expected to do frontier research on data quality, running experiments that will push forward our understanding of how data moves model performance. We're looking for people motivated by seeing their research move a system forward, with strong technical opinions, weakly held.

What You’ll Do:

  • Design and run experiments on training robotics, vision, and embodied AI models using Trace's real-world data.

  • Investigate how data quality, structure, and diversity affect downstream model performance, and turn those findings into concrete recommendations for what we capture.

  • Build and iterate on evaluation methodology so we know whether a model, or a dataset, is actually getting better.

  • Stay close to the literature on robot learning and translate what's relevant into work we can actually ship.

  • Work directly with the engineering and data teams so research findings turn into pipeline and product changes.

Who You Are:

  • Currently completing, or recently completed, a Master's or PhD program with a research focus on robot learning, robotics, or training foundation/AI models.

    • Exceptional undergraduates from top-tier robotics programs will also be considered.

  • No industry experience required. You can join us straight out of your program.

  • If you're coming from industry rather than a research program, your background should be a researcher role at a robotics company or an equally reputable research lab. General industry engineering experience without a research track record isn't a fit for this role.

  • Motivated by seeing research translate into working systems

  • Optimistic and serious about where robotics and AI are headed.

  • Comfortable being early in your career but still forming strong, defensible technical opinions.

Bonus:

  • Publications or research work specifically in robot learning or training models for physical/embodied systems

  • Experience from a leading robotics research program or lab

  • Hands-on exposure to real robotic hardware or real-world (versus purely simulated) data

jobs.title: Research Intern
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Trace

 

Trace is building the data, infrastructure, and research that enable robots to learn from the real world. General-purpose robotics requires a deeper understanding of how robots learn from real-world data. Our research explores how to transform human experiences, including egocentric video, demonstrations, hand-object interactions, and multimodal sensory signals, into transferable representations, actionable knowledge, and generalizable robot behaviors. At our Brooklyn research lab, we combine fundamental research in robot learning, computer vision, and embodied AI with large-scale datasets, machine learning infrastructure, and real-world robotic experimentation. Our goal is to advance the science of robot learning while developing the datasets and learning foundations for increasingly capable, adaptable, and reliable robots.

 
 

About the role

 

We are looking for highly motivated Research Interns to join our research team and work on challenging, high-impact problems at the intersection of robot learning, embodied AI, and learning from human experience. This internship is designed for PhD students and exceptional Master's students who are passionate about advancing the state of the art in robotics and machine learning.

 
 

As a Research Intern, you will take ownership of a focused research project, working closely with our scientists and engineers to formulate research questions, develop novel methods, design rigorous experiments, and evaluate results using real-world datasets, simulation, and/or robotic platforms. We encourage ambitious, scientifically grounded research with the potential to contribute to top-tier robotics, machine learning, and computer vision conferences. You will have opportunities to pursue original research, collaborate with an interdisciplinary team, and help shape Trace's long-term research directions.

 
 

Research areas

 

Research projects may span one or more of the following areas, but are not limited to:

 
 

• Learning from Human Experience and Egocentric Data

 

• Human-to-Robot and Cross-Embodiment Transfer

 

• Foundation Models for Robot Learning

 

• Visual-Tactile and Multimodal Robot Learning

 

• Data-Centric Robot Learning and Scaling

 

• Dexterous Manipulation and Generalizable Robot Skills

 

• Robustness, Generalization, and Reliable Robot Learning

 
 

We particularly welcome candidates who bring novel perspectives, strong methodological expertise, or creative research ideas that complement these directions.

 
 

What you'll do

 

• Lead an original research project from problem formulation and hypothesis development through method design, implementation, experimentation, and evaluation, with guidance and collaboration from Trace's research team.

 

• Develop and evaluate novel robot learning methods, including learning algorithms, representations, models, or training strategies that leverage human demonstrations, multimodal datasets, and robotic interaction data.

 

• Design rigorous experiments and benchmarks to investigate fundamental questions about data quality, human-to-robot transfer, policy learning, generalization, and real-world robotic performance.

 

• Work with diverse data modalities, potentially including egocentric video, human hand and body motion, teleoperation demonstrations, visual-tactile signals, force measurements, and robot trajectories.

 

• Collaborate with research scientists and engineers to build reproducible experimental pipelines, train and evaluate models, and validate research findings in simulation and/or on real robotic platforms.

 

• Analyze experimental results and failure modes, draw actionable scientific insights, and communicate findings through technical discussions, presentations, and written reports.

 

• Contribute to high-quality research publications and open research artifacts, with opportunities to submit work to leading robotics and machine learning venues.

 
 

What we're looking for

 

• Currently pursuing a PhD or Master's degree in Robotics, Machine Learning, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related field.

 

• Strong research background in at least one relevant area, such as robot learning, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, computer vision, embodied AI, foundation models, dexterous manipulation, multimodal learning, or learning from human demonstrations.

 

• Demonstrated research excellence and potential, evidenced by high-quality publications, impactful research projects, open-source contributions, or other substantial research accomplishments. Publications at leading venues such as RSS, CoRL, ICRA, IROS, T-RO, IJRR, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, or CVPR are highly valued. First-author or co-first-author publications are a strong plus.

 

• Excellent programming skills in Python and hands-on experience with modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX. Experience with C++ and parallel programming, such as CUDA, is a plus.

 

• Strong communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, interdisciplinary research environment.

 
 

Nice to have

 

• Experience with real-world robot learning experiments, robotic manipulation platforms, or deployment of learned policies on physical robots.

 

• Experience with egocentric video, human demonstrations, hand tracking, pose estimation, motion retargeting, or cross-embodiment learning.

 

• Experience with vision-language-action models, diffusion-based policies, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, or world models.

 

• Experience with tactile sensing, force estimation, multimodal sensor fusion, or contact-rich manipulation.

 

• Experience with robotics simulation environments and tools such as MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, or related frameworks.

 

• Previous research experience in an industrial research lab or a collaborative, interdisciplinary research environment.

 
 

How to apply

 

Please submit your CV/resume, along with links to your Google Scholar profile, personal website, GitHub, or other relevant research portfolio, if available. Internship start dates are flexible. Academic credit may be available if required by your degree program, subject to institutional requirements.

 
 

Trace is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.title: Robotics Engineering Intern — Hardware & Software
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Trace

Trace is building the data, infrastructure, and research that enable robots to learn from the real world. General-purpose robotics requires a deeper understanding of how robots learn from real-world data. Our research explores how to transform human experiences, including egocentric video, demonstrations, hand-object interactions, and multimodal sensory signals, into transferable representations, actionable knowledge, and generalizable robot behaviors. At our Brooklyn research lab, we combine fundamental research in robot learning, computer vision, and embodied AI with large-scale datasets, machine learning infrastructure, and real-world robotic experimentation. Our goal is to advance the science of robot learning while developing the datasets and learning foundations for increasingly capable, adaptable, and reliable robots.

About the role

We are looking for highly motivated and technically curious Robotics Engineering Interns to join our team in a hands-on hardware-and-software role, contributing to the development of robotic systems, data infrastructure, and experimental platforms that support cutting-edge research in robot learning and embodied AI. This internship is designed primarily for Master's and undergraduate students, although PhD students are also welcome to apply. We value practical robotics experience, strong engineering fundamentals, problem-solving ability, and a genuine interest in robotics research. Prior research publications are not required.

As a Robotics Engineering Intern, you will work closely with our research scientists, research interns, and engineers to build and operate robotic platforms, develop reliable data collection and processing pipelines, implement and evaluate learning-based robotic systems, and support experiments that connect human and robot data to downstream policy performance. You will have opportunities to take ownership of well-defined engineering and experimental projects, from hardware and software integration through implementation, testing, evaluation, and documentation. Depending on your background and interests, you may also contribute to research experiments, algorithm development, and technical publications. Our goal is to provide meaningful hands-on experience at the intersection of robotics engineering and robot learning research, while giving students opportunities to develop practical skills, deepen their research understanding, and contribute to advances in physical AI.

Projects you may work on

Depending on your experience and interests, your projects may involve one or more of the following areas:

  • Robotic Hardware and System Integration

  • Multimodal Data Collection and Infrastructure

  • Data Processing, Calibration, and Quality Evaluation

  • Human Demonstration and Robot Learning Systems

  • Robot Policy Implementation and Evaluation

  • Simulation and Experimental Validation

We welcome students with diverse technical backgrounds. You do not need prior experience in every area, and projects will be matched to your skills, interests, and available opportunities.

What you’ll learn and build

  • Build and integrate robotic systems, working with robot arms, dexterous hands, sensors, cameras, and associated software and hardware interfaces.

  • Develop and maintain robotics software and data pipelines for data acquisition, synchronization, processing, storage, visualization, and experimental evaluation.

  • Support robot learning research experiments by implementing existing methods, preparing datasets, running model training or evaluation, and executing experiments in simulation and/or on real robotic platforms.

  • Design and execute systematic tests to assess hardware reliability, sensor accuracy, data quality, policy performance, and experimental reproducibility.

  • Debug and troubleshoot complex robotic systems, identifying issues across hardware, perception, control, data processing, and learning components.

  • Analyze experimental results and failure cases, helping the research team understand how system design, data collection, and implementation choices affect robotic learning and performance.

  • Collaborate with researchers and engineers to improve experimental workflows, prototype new capabilities, and translate research ideas into functioning robotic systems.

  • Document implementations, experimental procedures, and results to support reproducibility, knowledge sharing, and continued development.

What we're looking for

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics, or a closely related field.

  • Solid programming skills in Python and/or C++, with experience developing, testing, or debugging software for robotics, machine learning, or related technical applications.

  • Foundational understanding of robotics concepts, such as robot kinematics, control, perception, sensing, or robotic system integration.

  • Hands-on experience with robotics hardware, simulation, or substantial robotics software projects, gained through coursework, research labs, internships, personal projects, or robotics competitions.

  • Strong practical problem-solving skills, willingness to learn unfamiliar tools and technologies, and ability to troubleshoot technical challenges independently.

  • Good communication and collaboration skills, attention to technical detail, and enthusiasm for working in a fast-paced, interdisciplinary research and engineering environment.

Nice to have

  • Experience with robotic platforms such as manipulators, dexterous hands, mobile robots, or humanoid robots, including hardware integration, control, or experimental deployment.

  • Familiarity with ROS/ROS 2, robot communication interfaces, motion planning, or robotic control software.

  • Experience with cameras, depth sensors, tactile sensors, force/torque sensors, motion capture systems, or multimodal sensor integration.

  • Experience with data acquisition, sensor calibration, temporal synchronization, data processing, or large-scale robotics datasets.

  • Familiarity with robot learning methods such as imitation learning, reinforcement learning, diffusion policies, or vision-language-action models.

  • Experience with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX, including training, fine-tuning, or evaluating learning-based models.

  • Experience with robotics simulation tools such as MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, or related environments.

  • Experience with CAD, mechanical prototyping, 3D printing, electronics, or embedded systems.

  • Previous experience in an academic robotics lab, robotics competition, engineering internship, or substantial independent robotics project.

  • Contributions to open-source robotics software, technical projects, datasets, or research publications are a plus, but not required.

How to apply

Please submit your resume/CV along with 1-3 examples of relevant technical or research work, such as GitHub repositories, project pages, robotics demonstration videos, open-source contributions, or publications. We encourage applicants to briefly describe their personal contributions to these projects, their technical interests, and what they hope to learn or accomplish during the internship.

Please indicate whether you are interested in a summer internship, a part-time internship during the academic year, or a full-time co-op opportunity. Internship start dates are flexible. Academic credit may be available if required by your degree program, subject to institutional requirements.

Trace is an equal opportunity employer.

Our goal is to provide meaningful hands-on experience at the intersection of robotics engineering and robot learning research, while giving students opportunities to develop practical skills, deepen their research understanding, and contribute to advances in physical AI.


PROJECTS YOU MAY WORK ON

Depending on your experience and interests, your projects may involve one or more of the following areas:

 - Robotic Hardware and System Integration

 - Multimodal Data Collection and Infrastructure

 - Data Processing, Calibration, and Quality Evaluation

 - Human Demonstration and Robot Learning Systems

 - Robot Policy Implementation and Evaluation

 - Simulation and Experimental Validation

We welcome students with diverse technical backgrounds. You do not need prior experience in every area, and projects will be matched to your skills, interests, and available opportunities.


WHAT YOU’LL LEARN AND BUILD

 - Build and integrate robotic systems, working with robot arms, dexterous hands, sensors, cameras, and associated software and hardware interfaces.

 - Develop and maintain robotics software and data pipelines for data acquisition, synchronization, processing, storage, visualization, and experimental evaluation.

 - Support robot learning research experiments by implementing existing methods, preparing datasets, running model training or evaluation, and executing experiments in simulation and/or on real robotic platforms.

 - Design and execute systematic tests to assess hardware reliability, sensor accuracy, data quality, policy performance, and experimental reproducibility.

 - Debug and troubleshoot complex robotic systems, identifying issues across hardware, perception, control, data processing, and learning components.

 - Analyze experimental results and failure cases, helping the research team understand how system design, data collection, and implementation choices affect robotic learning and performance.

 - Collaborate with researchers and engineers to improve experimental workflows, prototype new capabilities, and translate research ideas into functioning robotic systems.

 - Document implementations, experimental procedures, and results to support reproducibility, knowledge sharing, and continued development.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics, or a closely related field.

 - Solid programming skills in Python and/or C++, with experience developing, testing, or debugging software for robotics, machine learning, or related technical applications.

 - Foundational understanding of robotics concepts, such as robot kinematics, control, perception, sensing, or robotic system integration.

 - Hands-on experience with robotics hardware, simulation, or substantial robotics software projects, gained through coursework, research labs, internships, personal projects, or robotics competitions.

 - Strong practical problem-solving skills, willingness to learn unfamiliar tools and technologies, and ability to troubleshoot technical challenges independently.

 - Good communication and collaboration skills, attention to technical detail, and enthusiasm for working in a fast-paced, interdisciplinary research and engineering environment.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with robotic platforms such as manipulators, dexterous hands, mobile robots, or humanoid robots, including hardware integration, control, or experimental deployment.

 - Familiarity with ROS/ROS 2, robot communication interfaces, motion planning, or robotic control software.

 - Experience with cameras, depth sensors, tactile sensors, force/torque sensors, motion capture systems, or multimodal sensor integration.

 - Experience with data acquisition, sensor calibration, temporal synchronization, data processing, or large-scale robotics datasets.

 - Familiarity with robot learning methods such as imitation learning, reinforcement learning, diffusion policies, or vision-language-action models.

 - Experience with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX, including training, fine-tuning, or evaluating learning-based models.

 - Experience with robotics simulation tools such as MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, or related environments.

 - Experience with CAD, mechanical prototyping, 3D printing, electronics, or embedded systems.

 - Previous experience in an academic robotics lab, robotics competition, engineering internship, or substantial independent robotics project.

 - Contributions to open-source robotics software, technical projects, datasets, or research publications are a plus, but not required.


HOW TO APPLY

Please submit your resume/CV along with 1-3 examples of relevant technical or research work, such as GitHub repositories, project pages, robotics demonstration videos, open-source contributions, or publications. We encourage applicants to briefly describe their personal contributions to these projects, their technical interests, and what they hope to learn or accomplish during the internship.

Please indicate whether you are interested in a summer internship, a part-time internship during the academic year, or a full-time co-op opportunity. Internship start dates are flexible. Academic credit may be available if required by your degree program, subject to institutional requirements.

Trace is an equal opportunity employer.
